source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM TERTIUM, De baptismo. Atque haec de sacramentis V.T.: sequuntur N.T. quae pro populo Christiano divinitus instituta per rem terrenam exhibent simul rem coelestem, ut credentibus gratiam Euangelii obsignent & conferant. II. Sacramenta N.T. sunt duo: BAPTISMUS & COENA DOMINI. Baptismus est sacramentum quo homo aqua in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus Sancti ablutus in foedus gratiae recipitur, peccatorum remissione, regeneratione & adoptione obsignatus (Matth. 28:19; Acts 2:38; Tit. 3:5).
english: Thus far Old Testament sacraments; there follow those of the New, divinely instituted for the Christian people, which through an earthly thing exhibit at once a heavenly thing, that they may seal and confer Gospel grace on believers.

II. New Testament sacraments are two: BAPTISM and the LORD'S SUPPER. Baptism is the sacrament by which a human washed with water in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit is received into the covenant of grace, sealed with remission of sins, regeneration, and adoption (Matt. 28:19; Acts 2:38; Tit. 3:5).

source_text: VII. Objectum baptismi est omnis homo qui foederi gratiae adscribi potest. VIII. Baptismus non est saepius iterandus. Baptismus Johannis a baptismo nostro quoad substantiam non differt: eadem materia (Matth. 3:11), eadem forma (John 1:33; Matth. 28:19). 2. Baptismus tantum a ministro Christi legitime vocato administrandus est. 3. Soli homines baptizandi sunt quotquot salvari possunt & debent.
english: VII. The object of baptism is every human who can be enrolled in the covenant of grace. VIII. Baptism is not to be iterated often.

John's baptism does not differ from ours as to substance: same matter (Matt. 3:11), same form (John 1:33; Matt. 28:19). Baptism is to be administered only by a lawfully called minister of Christ. Only humans who can and ought to be saved are to be baptized.

source_text: 4. Infantes parentum tam fidelium quam infidelium baptizandi sunt, non ob carnis generationem aut merita parentum, sed ob promissionem gratiae foederi adhaerentem (Gen. 17; Acts 2:39; 1 Cor. 7:14). 5. Infantes recte baptizantur in novo testamento, sicut pueri circumciduntur in veteri—quia eadem promissio & foedus, idem Christus, eadem fides parentum foederatorum.
english: 4. Infants of both believing and unbelieving parents are to be baptized—not because of fleshly generation or parents' merits, but because of the promise of grace adhering to the covenant (Gen. 17; Acts 2:39; 1 Cor. 7:14).
5. Infants are rightly baptized in the New Testament as boys were circumcised in the Old—because the same promise and covenant, the same Christ, and the same faith of covenanted parents.

source_text: 6. Ritus baptismi a Deo instituti ad eius integritatem pertinent: ablutio aqua, invocatio Trinitatis; accessoria sunt catechisatio adultorum, impositio nominis, patrini sive susceptores. 7. Aqua baptismi regenerat & renovat non virtute sua naturali, sed supernaturali operatione & adiuncto verbo sacrosanctae Trinitatis (1 Pet. 3:20-21; Eph. 5:26; Tit. 3:5; John 3:5). 8. Fructus baptismi adultis per fidem actualem, infantibus ante annos discretionis decedentibus a Spiritu S. tanquam fidei causa principe applicatur. 9. Etiamsi baptismus semel tantum suscipiatur, tamen servit nobis per omnem vitam ad fidei robur, confirmationem adversus tentationes, & diligentiam in cultu Dei.
english: 6. Rites of baptism instituted by God belong to its integrity: washing with water and invocation of the Trinity; accessories include catechizing of adults, naming, and sponsors.
7. Baptismal water regenerates and renews not by its natural power but by supernatural operation and the adjoining word of the holy Trinity (1 Pet. 3:20-21; Eph. 5:26; Tit. 3:5; John 3:5).

8. Baptism's fruit is applied to adults through actual faith, and to infants dying before years of discretion by the Holy Spirit as principal cause of faith. 9. Though received only once, baptism serves us through all life for strength of faith, confirmation against temptations, and diligence in God's worship.

source_text: 10. Si quis vel ex ecclesiae vel parentum vel aliorum testimonio de baptismo in infantia accepto certus esse nequeat: is sine scrupulo baptizandus est. Nam concilio Carthaginensi 5 cap. 3: Placuit de infantibus... absque ullo scrupulo esse baptizandos. Ut Leo recte addit, iteratum dici non potest quod nescitur esse factum. CAPUT DECIMUM QUARTUM sequitur, De coena Domini.
english: 10. If anyone cannot be sure from the testimony of church, parents, or others that he received baptism in infancy, he is to be baptized without scruple. The fifth Council of Carthage rightly decided that such infants are to be baptized without scruple. As Leo rightly adds, what is not known to have been done cannot be called iterated.
CHAPTER FOURTEEN follows, On the Lord's Supper.
